title: Daily Debrief — Tuesday Nov 3, 2026
html:
SPY held our line to the penny. Now the voters get a say.

Chips finally bounced today, and AMD and Super Micro both jumped after the bell. But tonight's midterm results can change the picture before tomorrow's open.

The one thing

SPY's low today was $752.39, right on our $752.30 line, and it closed at $754.35. Buyers defended it. A close above $757 opens the $763.50–768 ceiling. A close below $743 still means we play defense.

The S&P 500 rose 0.4%, the Nasdaq 0.8%, and the Dow fell 0.4%. Chips did the lifting (SMH +2.0%, NVDA +2.3%, AMD +3.7%). AAPL fell 1.9% after a soft margin forecast. Brent eased to about $103–104 on hopes for US–Iran talks. The 10-year yield rose to about 4.95% after two Fed presidents said rates may need to rise (Fed Tracker, Federal Reserve). After the close, AMD beat (revenue $13.4B, data center +97%, Q4 guide about $17B) and rose about 7.6% to near $520. Super Micro reported $19.9B in revenue and rose about 7.7%.

SPY levels

  • Record high: $781.62 (Oct 6)
  • Ceiling: $763.50–768 (23.6% + 20-day + 50-day)
  • First lid: $757 (today's high + 0.786× extension)
  • The line: $752.30 (38.2% + 1.0× extension) — held today, low $752.39
  • Support: $743–748 (Sep 16 low + 50% + 23.6% of the big run + 1.382×)
  • Next: $731–734 (61.8% + 2.0×)
  • Floor: $721–727 (200-day $726.65 + 78.6% + 38.2% of the big run + 2.382×)

How I read it: buyers defended the line but couldn't get past $757. Prediction markets gave Democrats about a 76% chance of winning both chambers, which some say isn't priced in, so tonight can gap SPY either way. A close below $743 turns me defensive; a close above $757, then $768, says the October pullback is done.

Your names that matter today

  • NVDA $206.69 (+2.3%, after hours ≈ $209.80) — READY ON TRIGGER. It held $200, so the put is off. It closed back above the 200-day ($204.27). Uptrend plus RSI 39 is the tested edge setup. Trigger: a daily close above $210.94 (23.6%), with a target of $217–218 (38.2% + 20-day). Cancel on a close below $204. Exit before Nov 17 earnings.
  • AMD $483.90 (+3.7%, after hours ≈ $520.70) — WAIT. A clean beat. After hours it's just under the 61.8% level ($523.78), with $549–550 (50-day + 50%) above. I want to see it hold the gap above about $505, then close above $523.78. IV is about 60%.
  • HLT $363.83 (−0.2%) — WAIT. It missed the second close above $364.50 by 67 cents. Entry is a close above $364.50 or a dip to $356–360 that holds. Cancel below $352.
  • RCL $313.17 (−2.5%) — WAIT, getting closer. RSI fell from 72 to 66. The $307–308 buy zone is 2% away, with $300.40 as the backstop.
  • Also: SMCI after hours ≈ $33.80, back above its 200-day. AAPL $331.90 sits under its 38.2% level ($332.19). PLTR $175.40 is holding the 78.6% level ($174.91). BA, DAL and NOW are unchanged. TSLA is down 1.3%. XOM is on its 20-day. DELL rose 4.0% after hours.

Lesson of the day: Delta

Delta is roughly how many cents an option gains per $1 the stock moves (×100 per contract), and a rough guide to the odds it finishes in the money. The NVDA Dec $220 call has a delta of 0.41, so it gains about $41 per $1 NVDA rises and costs about $728. The RCL Dec $360 call has a delta of 0.19, so it gains about $19 per $1 and costs about $340, but RCL needs to rise about $50 just to break even. That's why the rule is delta ≥ 0.20. A $10 NVDA move to $217 should add about $400 to the $220 call, before time decay.

Plays on deck (Options Playbook)

  1. NVDA Dec 18 $220 call — ≈ $728, Δ 0.41 (live mid $7.28). Enter on a daily close above $210.94. Exit on a close below $204 or near $217–218, and be out before Nov 17.
  2. HLT Dec 18 $380 call — ≈ $670, Δ 0.33 (spread $5.60–7.80, use a limit order). Enter on a close above $364.50 or a held dip to $356–360. Exit on a close below $352. Target $385.90.
  3. RCL Dec 18 $340 call — ≈ $800 now, about $600 on the dip (estimate, verify in Webull), Δ 0.32. Enter on a dip to $307–308 that closes back above it. Exit on a close below $300. Target $324.55, then $327.

Skip: chasing the AMD/SMCI gap, the cancelled NVDA put, new trades before the election settles, and lottery tickets under 0.20 delta.

Homework

  1. Check SPY's first 30 minutes against $752.30 and $757. If it gaps, does the gap hold by 10:00 a.m.?
  2. Find delta on the NVDA Dec 18 $220 call in Webull, and compare its move to NVDA's at the close.

Question: If AMD opens at $520 and fades to $505 by noon, what does that tell you about buyers, and would you still want the NVDA call?
